This indexes the SECOND character (lower[1]) instead of the FIRST (lower[0]), so the first letter of each word is dropped and the second letter is uppercased while also being duplicated by slice(1). For "hello big world": "big" → 'I'+'ig' = "Iig" (should be "Big"), "world" → 'O'+'orld' = "Oorld" (should be "World"), producing "helloIigOorld" instead of "helloBigWorld". The fix is to use `lower[0].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1)`.

payload.rationale: The root cause is an off-by-one string index in camelCase at src/text.js:41. Words after the first are capitalized via `lower[1].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1)`, which uppercases the SECOND character while slice(1) keeps the second character onward — so the first letter is dropped and the second is duplicated/uppercased (e.g. "big" -> "Iig"). Changing the index from `lower[1]` to `lower[0]` makes it uppercase the first character and append the rest via slice(1) (e.g. "big" -> "B" + "ig" = "Big"), so "hello big world" now yields "helloBigWorld" as documented and asserted by test/text.test.js:25. This is the smallest possible change (one character) and touches no other behavior.
